environment_findings: source captures are 100% image, zero text layer - pdftotext returns 0 words
sqlite3 CLI not installed; use Python sqlite3 module
SQLite throws 'no such collation sequence: unicase' - must register before any query
python-docx 1.2.0 and docx-js (node) both available; docx-js used for NOTES builds
Drive: use download_file_content + base64 decode for JSON/scripts. read_file_content markdown-escapes output and breaks json.loads().

incidents.issue: Image rendering degraded mid-session and never recovered
incidents.detail: Pages 1, 8, 18, 28, 38, 46 rendered fine early. Every subsequent view returned blank, including re-reads of files that had already worked. Text tooling unaffected throughout.
incidents.mitigation: Front-load the visual read as the first action of every session. Fall back to OCR + pdfimages if it fails.

incidents.issue: Validation false positives from field concatenation
incidents.detail: Concatenating Text+Extra without a separator manufactured 59 fake run-on errors in a deck that had 2 real ones.
incidents.mitigation: Always audit each field separately. Never glue fields together for regex checks.

incidents.issue: Silent edit failure on HTML-wrapped text
incidents.detail: A fix targeting 'LAST.' did nothing because the card read 'LAST is a major concern'. Would have shipped unfixed.
incidents.mitigation: Gate must log SKIP when a pattern is not found, and the build must assert edits_applied == edits_intended.

incidents.issue: build_deck.py --patch deleted the file it was about to read
incidents.detail: The media-preservation fix reads the source archive's member list to carry the 90 blobs forward, but did `os.remove(apkg_path)` first. On --patch, SRC IS apkg_path - the deck is patched in place - so the script destroyed its own source and died with FileNotFoundError after already overwriting the .txt. No patch could ever have completed on this code path.
incidents.mitigation: Read the member list and blob inventory BEFORE touching the destination. Fixed 2026-07-30. selftest now covers --patch (section 4d), which is the gap that let this ship.

incidents.issue: A patch overwrote the build's changelog, silently gutting the NOTES doc
incidents.detail: build_deck.py wrote work/<module>/changelog.json with only the patch's entries. build_notes.js reads that file, so rebuilding NOTES after a patch produced a 12 KB doc with 0 IO requests and 0 adds - all 179 build entries and 5 embedded figures gone. Caught only because the file size looked wrong.
incidents.mitigation: The changelog now accumulates on --patch, reading prior entries from scratch or from COMPLETED/<module>/audit/ and deduplicating. `changelog` itself is left unmerged so the ops-applied gate still counts against len(OPS). Fixed 2026-07-30.

incidents.issue: PROMPT_verify.md and build_deck.py disagree on the patch input path
incidents.detail: The prompt says write _work/<module>/patch_ops.json; build_deck.py reads work/<module>/. A session following the prompt literally gets 'Nothing to do: no ops and no cards found'.
incidents.mitigation: Fixed 2026-07-30: the prompts were wrong, not the scripts. Every executable (build_deck.py WORKROOT, next_action.py WORK, cleanup.py, verify_deck.py, selftest.py, build_notes.js) resolves 'work/' next to the scripts, so all five PROMPT_*.md files and handoff_template.md now say work/<module>/ too. The only surviving '_work' references are '<path>/_work' cleanup examples, which point at the legacy Drive scratch root and are correct. handoff_template.md 4e explains the distinction.

incidents.issue: Two silent infinite loops in the unattended orchestrator, neither covered by any test
incidents.detail: next_action.py resolved COMPLETED/ as HERE/COMPLETED, but every scheduled run copies the scripts to a fresh scratch dir where that does not exist, so has_verify_report() always returned False and VERIFY was re-issued on an already-verified module every run, forever. Separately, build_queue.py excluded only 'verified' modules from the queue; since a finished module rests at 'built-unverified' until the user runs --pass, refreshing the queue each run would have re-queued it and rebuilt it from scratch, discarding the verification. Neither could be seen from outside: both look like the pipeline working.
incidents.mitigation: next_action.py now resolves COMPLETED as env COMPLETED_DIR -> paths.completed in project_state.json -> HERE/COMPLETED, re-validates that the chosen path exists, and exits 2 with an explanation rather than guessing when none resolve. It also refuses to issue BUILD for a queued deck whose .apkg is missing. build_queue.py now excludes every tracked module regardless of status, resolves its input dirs as argv -> env -> recorded -> default, and records project_root/source_dir/deck_dir/completed for later runs. selftest.py sections 6 and 7 cover the whole decision table and the multi-deck loop - there was no coverage of next_action.py or build_queue.py at all before, which is how both shipped.

incidents.issue: --pass marked a module verified but silently failed to archive its inputs
incidents.detail: verify_deck.py --pass invoked archive_inputs.py with ANKI_DECK_DIR/SOURCE_DIR/ARCHIVE_DIR defaulting to relative paths ('Anki Decks', ...). A --pass runs from a local scratch copy where those resolve to nothing, and the call used check=False inside a bare try/except, so it printed nothing and moved nothing. The original deck stayed in Anki Decks/ - which archive_inputs.py exists specifically to prevent, because a later run can then take an already-optimized deck as its source and gap-fill it twice. Separately, --pass called update_handoff.regenerate() before archiving, and render_status raised KeyError on a module record missing an optional field, aborting the pass after the status flip but before the file moves.
incidents.mitigation: verify_deck.py --pass now resolves the three folders as env -> paths recorded in project_state.json -> conventional default, validates the deck folder exists, and after archiving re-checks that the deck actually left the input folder, reporting loudly if it did not. build_queue.py records paths.archive_dir alongside the others. update_handoff.render_status uses .get throughout, and --pass wraps regenerate() so a handoff-rendering failure can never block the file moves. selftest.py section 8 covers the whole path end to end.
